title: De Loera–Lee–Margulies–Miller conjecture on minor-minimal non-weakly-orientable matroids
statement:
Let $M\!I_n$ be the infinite family of matroids constructed in the paper, indexed by integers $n\geq 0$. A matroid is **weakly orientable** when its Bland–Jensen linear system has a solution over $F_2$; it is **minor-minimal non-weakly-orientable** when it is non-weakly orientable but every proper minor is weakly orientable. The authors conjecture that

**Minor-minimality conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq 0$, $M\!I_n$ are minor-minimal with respect to being non-weakly-orientable. Hence, weak-orientability cannot be described by a finite list of excluded minors.

The family $M\!I_n$ is an infinite family of non-weakly-orientable matroids with growing rank and corank. The authors checked explicitly that $M\!I_n$ is minor-minimal for $n\leq 2$; the conjecture would imply the earlier Bland–Jensen conjecture that weak orientability cannot be characterized by a finite list of excluded minors.
source_name: J. A. De Loera, J. Lee, S. Margulies and J. Miller, “Weak Orientability of Matroids and Polynomial Equations”, arXiv:1309.7719 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.7719

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).
